text.p: Austrian high-grade steel maker Boehler-Uddeholm said on Tuesday it was cautious on the outlook for the current year as market conditions remained weak.
"A stagnant economy in some of the group's core markets give reason to be cautious on the outlook for 1997," it said in a statement released ahead of a news conference.
"Management expects earnings growth to slow down at least in the first half of 1997, a significant increase in high-grade steel market conditions is only expected toward the end of 1997," it added.

On the positive side, the group noted it expected higher export margins and an increase in market share for the current year. Incoming orders in the first two months of the year were already five percent above last year's level, it said. -- Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
